chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sukuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

The meal is perfected when it gathers four traits: if it is from what is permissible (halal); the number of hands upon it are many; Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, is named at its beginning; and that He is praised at its end.

key_terms.السُّكُونِيِّ: A specific narrator from the Banu Sukun tribe

ai.seo_question: What are the four conditions that make a meal perfect in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this chain from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the interplay between ritual purity (halal) and social cohesion (katharat al-aydi). This narration elevates the mundane act of eating into a spiritual practice where divine invocation transforms sustenance into a blessing, reflecting the Imams' teachings on the sanctity of daily life.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Musa bin Mutawakkil, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim bin Hashim, from his father, from Abdullah bin Mughaira, from Isma’eel bin Muslim al-Sukuni, from Ja’far bin Muhammed, from his father, from his fathers, from Ali, peace be upon him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said:

If the meal has gathered four traits, it is perfected: if it is from what is allowable; the number of hands upon it are many; Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, is named at its beginning; and that He is praised at its end.
